hexagrams.name: The Creative

wangbi.judgment:
"Heaven" is the name of the form. "Vigor" is what employs the form. Now form is the encumbrance of things. To have the form of Heaven and be able to preserve it forever without diminishment, to be the foremost of things — is not that which governs it the ultimate in vigor? Greatly illuminating the Way of ending and beginning, therefore the six positions do not miss their proper time and are completed. Rising and descending without constancy, employed according to the time — when at rest, one rides the submerged dragon; when emerging, one rides the flying dragon — therefore it says 'riding the six dragons in due season.' Riding transformation and change to drive the great vessel, still and focused when at rest, straight and direct when in motion, never losing the Great Harmony — is this not what correctly establishes the genuine nature of all things' natures and destinies?

Without harmony there is rigidity and violence.

The reason the myriad states are at peace is that each has its ruler.

hexagrams.name: The Receptive

wangbi.judgment:
What Kun’s steadfastness benefits is the mare. The horse moves upon the ground below, and being female, it is the utmost of compliance. Only through utmost compliance does one attain success; therefore it benefits only the steadfastness of a mare.

The southwest is the region of nourishment, sharing the same Way as Kun; hence it says ‘one finds companions.’ The northeast is the opposite of the southwest; hence it says ‘one loses companions.’ The nature of yin is that it must leave its own kind and go toward the opposite kind, and only then does it attain peaceful steadfastness and good fortune.

lines.1: It begins with treading on frost and reaches solid ice—this is what is meant by ‘utmost softness yet moving toward hardness.’ The Way of yin is rooted in the humble and weak and only later accumulates to prominence; therefore it takes ‘treading on frost’ to illuminate its beginning. Yang as a force is not one that builds from a beginning to reach prominence; therefore it is illuminated through eme
lines.2: Dwelling in the center and attaining correctness, it reaches the utmost of Earth’s substance. Entrusting itself to the natural, things arise of themselves; without relying on cultivation or contrivance, accomplishments are completed of themselves. Therefore, without practice, nothing is unfavorable.
lines.3: The third position occupies the extreme of the lower trigram, yet is not suspected by yang—it corresponds to this meaning. lines.4: Situated in a yin hexagram, occupying a yin position with a yin line, treading upon a position that is not central—it lacks the substance of straightness and squareness. Not undertaking yang affairs, it lacks the beauty of containing pattern. Tying shut and blocking closed—the worthy person goes into hiding. Exercising caution is acceptable, but this is not the Way of flourishing.
lines.5: Yellow is the color of the center. The lower garment is the adornment of what is below. Kun represents the Way of the minister, whose beauty is fully expressed in the subordinate position. Without the substance of firm strength, yet able to fathom the dispositions of all things—this is one who comprehends principle. With the virtue of yielding compliance, occupying a flourishing position, and entr
lines.6: The Way of yin is that through humility, compliance, and not overflowing, it preserves its beauty intact. When it waxes full and does not cease, it encroaches upon yang’s territory, which yang cannot endure—therefore they battle in the open field.

The firm and the yielding first begin to interact—this is why there is difficulty. If they did not interact, there would be obstruction; therefore difficulty leads to great success. With great success there is no danger; therefore it is beneficial to be correct.

hexagrams.name: Youthful Folly

wangbi.judgment:
Divination is a means for resolving doubt. The young fool comes seeking me because he desires to resolve his perplexity. If the resolution is not singular, he will not know which course to follow and will become perplexed again. Therefore, at the first consultation one gives instruction; at the second or third, it becomes importunity — importuning the one in darkness. The one capable of being the 'first consultation' is surely the second line? With firmness dwelling in the center, it is able to decide doubt.

What benefits Youthful Folly is beneficial correctness. Nothing is brighter than the sage; nothing is darker than the fool. To use folly to nurture correctness — this is the work of the sage. But to nurture correctness through manifest brilliance would be to lose the Way.

hexagrams.name: Treading

zh: 言乎一卦之所以為主也

wangbi.judgment:
In general, the Tuan speaks of what constitutes the ruling principle of the entire hexagram; the constitutive body of this hexagram lies in Six in the Third. 'Treading upon the tiger's tail' speaks of its danger. The Third is the ruling line of Lü; being soft it treads upon the firm—one who treads upon danger. Treading upon the tiger's tail yet not being bitten is because it is joyous and responds to Qian. Qian represents the virtue of firmness and correctness. Not using joyousness to practice flattery and wickedness, but using joyousness to respond to Qian—it is fitting that one treads upon the tiger's tail without being bitten, and attains success.

This speaks of the virtue of the Fifth.

lines.1: Occupying the beginning of Lü, this is the start of treading. The way of treading abhors ornamentation; therefore plainness brings no blame. If one conducts treading with plainness, where can one go without compliance? One surely carries out one's wishes independently, and nothing violates it.

Setting one's will on firmness and strength without cultivating what one treads up
lines.4: Pressing close to the most honored position, yang supporting yang, dwelling in a place of much apprehension—therefore it says 'treading upon the tiger's tail, apprehensive and cautious.' However, being yang dwelling in a yin position, one takes humility as the foundation. Although dwelling in danger and apprehension, one ultimately attains one's aim; therefore in the end there is good fortune.
lines.5: Attaining the position and dwelling in eminence, deciding with firmness and correctness—therefore it says 'resolute treading, correctness brings danger.' The way of treading abhors excess, yet the Fifth dwells in eminence; this is why there is danger.

hexagrams.name: Following

wangbi.judgment: Zhen is the firm and Dui is the yielding. When the firm places itself below the yielding, and there is movement toward joy, then Following is achieved. To have Following without great free passage is to go against the time. To follow one another without Benefit and Correctness is the way of disaster. Therefore, only with great free passage, Benefit, and Correctness can there be no blame. To have Following that brings about great free passage, Benefit, and Correctness is to accord with the time; when one accords with the time, all under heaven follows. What Following enacts depends solely on the time. When the time changes and one does not follow, that is the way of obstruction. Therefore, how great is the meaning of following the time!

lines.1: Occupying the beginning of Following, above there is no corresponding line, and there is no partial attachment. en: Dwelling in the noble position, serving as the master of Contemplation, broadly proclaiming the great transforming influence, its radiance reaching the four quarters—this is the ultimate of Contemplation

wangbi.judgment: Of what is worthy of contemplation in the way of the king, nothing surpasses the ancestral temple. Of what is worthy of contemplation in the ancestral temple, nothing surpasses the ablution. When it comes to the offering of food, it is simple and insufficient for further contemplation; therefore one contemplates the ablution but does not contemplate the offering. Confucius said: 'As for the di sacrifice, from after the libation onward, I have no wish to observe it.' When one fully contemplates the grandeur, those below contemplate it and are transformed. Therefore, when contemplation reaches the ablution, there is sincerity, dignified and reverent.

hexagrams.name: Grace

en: Occupying the honored position, it is the master of adornment—the most flourishing in adornment

wangbi.judgment:
If firm and yielding are not apportioned, how can pattern arise? Therefore Kun's top six comes to occupy the second position—this is the meaning of 'the yielding comes to embellish the firm.' The yielding comes to embellish the firm and occupies a position that attains the center; this is why there is Success. Qian's nine in the second is apportioned to occupy the top position—this is the meaning of 'the firm is apportioned upward to embellish the yielding.' The firm goes up to embellish the yielding but does not attain the central position, which is not as good as the yielding coming to embellish the firm; hence 'small benefit in having somewhere to go.'

Firm and yielding interlace to form pattern—this is the pattern of Heaven.

Bringing things to rest not through military force but through civilized brightness—this is the pattern of humanity.

If one understands the patterns of Heaven, then the changes of the seasons can be known; if one understands the patterns of humanity, then transformation and perfection can be achieved.

lines.1: At the beginning of Adornment, with firmness dwelling below, he occupies a position without rank. He renounces what is not righteous and is content to go on foot in order to follow his aspiration. Therefore he adorns his toes, leaves the carriage and goes on foot—this means that in righteousness he does not ride.
lines.2: It has attained its proper position but lacks a correlate. The Third also lacks a correlate. Both lack correlates yet are adjacent—they are close and find affinity with each other. The beard as a thing is something that attaches above. Following what it treads upon to attach itself to what is above, hence it says 'he adorns his beard.'
lines.3: Occupying the extreme of the lower body, it dwells in its proper position and is adjacent to the Second. Both tread upon what is correct; they harmonize together and moisten each other, thereby completing their pattern. Having achieved both adornment and moisture, hence it says 'adorned and glistening.' Eternally maintaining its correctness, nothing can encroach upon it; hence it says 'perpetual c
lines.4: It has a correlate in the Initial line but is obstructed by the Third, which creates hostile difficulty for it. The two aspirations resonate with each other but cannot achieve free passage. If it wishes to remain still, it doubts* the Initial line's response; if it wishes to advance, it fears the Third line's difficulty. Therefore it is sometimes adorned, sometimes plain—inwardly harboring doubt a
lines.5: Occupying the honored position, it is the master of adornment—the most flourishing in adornment. If one lavishes adornment upon things, its Way causes harm. But to bestow adornment upon hills and gardens—nothing is more magnificent. Therefore, if one adorns with rolls of silk, the hills and gardens will decline; but if one adorns in the manner of hills and gardens, the silk remains abundant and sl
lines.6: Dwelling at the end of Adornment, when adornment reaches its end it returns to the plain. Therefore it rests in its plain simplicity, not laboring over embellishment, and is without blame. Using white as adornment, without worry or distress—this is one who has attained his aspiration.

hexagrams.name: Innocence

en: Dwelling in the honored position, this is the ruler of Without Falseness
The firm comes from without and becomes the ruler within
What could this be if not great success through benefit and correctness? When the firm comes from without and becomes the ruler within, then the way of the soft and deviant is eliminated

wangbi.judgment:
This refers to Zhen.

Zhen moves and Qian is strong.

This refers to the fifth line.

The firm comes from without and becomes the ruler within; moving, it grows ever stronger. Firm, centered, and having a correspondent—authoritative, firm, upright, and correct—selfish desires cannot prevail. How could there be falseness? It causes the way of falseness to be extinguished and the way of Without Falseness to be accomplished. What could this be if not great success through benefit and correctness? When the firm comes from without and becomes the ruler within, then the way of the soft and deviant is eliminated. When moving it grows ever stronger, then the way of the firm and upright prevails. When it is firm, centered, and has a correspondent, then the virtue of order and clarity is made manifest. Therefore there is great success through correctness. The teaching mandate of Heaven—how can it be violated? How can there be falseness? This is why if one is not correct there will be calamity, and it is not beneficial to have a place to go.

If one is not correct and there is calamity, yet one does not seek to reform and follow correctness but instead wishes to go somewhere—dwelling in a time when one must not be false, yet wishing to go somewhere through incorrectness—where does one intend to go? What the mandate of Heaven does not protect is finished indeed!

lines.1: Its substance is firm and it dwells below, using nobility to descend to the lowly. Its conduct does not transgress into falseness; therefore in going forth it attains its aim.
lines.2: Not plowing yet reaping, not clearing yet having mature land—one completes what another began and does not initiate. Not claiming the merit for oneself, one fully fulfills the way of the minister; therefore it is beneficial to have a place to go.
lines.3: Occupying a yang position with a yin line, its conduct violates humility and compliance; this is why Without Falseness results in disaster. The ox is the resource for farming. The second line, by not plowing yet reaping, found it beneficial to have a place to go. But the third line engages in non-compliant conduct; therefore someone tethers its ox. This is how the official gains an acquisition and
lines.4: Dwelling in a time of Without Falseness, occupying a yin position with a yang line, the firm rides upon the yielding. Treading the path of humility and compliance and being close to the supreme ruler, one may therefore undertake what is correct, firmly maintaining what one holds, and so there is no blame.
lines.5: Dwelling in the honored position, this is the ruler of Without Falseness. Those below are all without falseness; the harm is not something one has caused. To take medicine in such a case would make the illness worse. A disaster that does not arise from falseness, if left untreated, will resolve on its own. To apply medicine to what is not false would bring misfortune; hence it says 'do not use med
lines.6: Dwelling at the extreme of the time when one must not be false, one should only remain still and preserve one's person. Therefore one must not take action.

hexagrams.name: Great Accumulation

en: The Fifth occupies the honored position and is the master of accumulation

wangbi.judgment:
In general, things that decline after being resisted are weak; things that fall after flourishing are insubstantial. Those able to radiate brilliance and daily renew their virtue are only the firm, strong, sincere, and substantial.

This refers to the Top Nine. It occupies the top position with great openness; the firm comes and it does not resist—this is what is meant by esteeming the worthy.

Nothing is stronger than Qian, yet it is able to halt it. Without great correctness, this could not be achieved.

Possessing the substance of great accumulation and using it to nourish the worthy, causing the worthy not to eat at home—this is auspicious. Esteeming the worthy and restraining the strong, with great correctness corresponding to Heaven, one does not worry about dangers and difficulties, hence benefit in crossing a great river.

lines.1:
The Fourth is the one accumulating it; it must not be opposed. Hence advancing brings danger, while stopping brings benefit.

Occupying the beginning of the strong, it has not yet fulfilled its strength, hence it is able to benefit from stopping.
lines.2: The Fifth occupies the height of accumulation and must not be opposed. Encountering this and still advancing, the cart therefore sheds its axle straps. Occupying the attainment of the center, able to use its centrality and not recklessly wade across the river—dying without regret—encountering difficulty it is able to stop, hence there is no blame.
lines.3: In general, when things reach their extreme they reverse, hence when accumulation reaches its extreme it opens up. The advance of the first and second lines meets the height of accumulation, so they cannot ascend. When it comes to Nine in the Third, it ascends to the Top Nine, and the Top Nine occupies the success of Heaven's thoroughfare—the path is wide open, with no opposition or resistance in
lines.4: Occupying the beginning of Gen, treading properly in its position, it is able to halt the strong Initial line. It resists not with horns; the yielding halts the firm, and the firm dares not oppose. Suppressing keenness at its inception to quell forceful contention—this is not merely beneficial alone; there will indeed be cause for joy.
lines.5: The tusks of a boar are recklessly violent—an object fierce, brutal, and difficult to control—this refers to the Second. The Fifth occupies the honored position and is the master of accumulation. The Second is firm and advances, yet it is able to geld its tusks. The yielding can control the strong, restraining violence and suppressing vigor. This is not merely able to secure its position; there wi
lines.6: Occupying the extreme of accumulation—when accumulation reaches its extreme it opens up—Great Accumulation has arrived at the time of great success. He (何) is an exclamatory particle, as if to say 'what further accumulation?'—it is now the success of Heaven's thoroughfare.

hexagrams.name: Influence

wangbi.judgment:
Therefore there is Success.

Hence Benefit in Correctness.

Taking a wife brings good fortune.

The two qi unite with each other, and thus transformation and birth occur.

The true nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things is seen in what influences them. In general, as a principle of influence, one cannot influence what is not of the same kind; therefore taking a wife is cited to illuminate the meaning of being of the same kind. When those of the same kind do not influence and respond to each other, it is because each holds itself aloof in its position. Therefore, although the female is the counterpart that corresponds to the male, one must lower oneself before her, and only then does taking a wife bring good fortune.

lines.1:
Occupying the beginning of Xian, this is the start of influence. What is influenced is at the extremity, so there is merely an intention and nothing more. As for its fundamental substance, it has not yet reached the point of disturbing stillness.

The fourth line belongs to the outer trigram.
lines.2: The Way of influence advances further: leaving the big toe and ascending to the calf. The calf as a body part is given to motion and restlessness. To influence things through restlessness is the path to misfortune. Because of restlessness there is misfortune; remaining still brings good fortune. lines.3: The thigh as a thing follows the foot. Advancing, it cannot control movement; retreating, it cannot remain quietly still. What is influenced being the thigh, the intention is to follow others. When the intention is to follow others, what one clings to is also base. To proceed on this basis—distress is fitting.
lines.4: Occupying the beginning of the upper trigram and corresponding with the beginning of the lower trigram, situated in the center of the body and above the thigh—this is where the two constituent trigrams first interact and influence each other to communicate their intentions. It is the point where the heart and spirit first experience influence. Whenever things first experience influence and one doe
lines.5: The mei (upper back flesh) is above the heart and below the mouth. Advancing, one cannot achieve great influence; retreating, one is not without intention either. The intention is shallow and at the periphery; therefore there is merely no regret.
lines.6:
The Way of influence has turned to its very end, therefore it resides merely in the mouth, tongue, and spoken words.

hexagrams.name: Retreat

wangbi.judgment:
The meaning of Retreat is that by retreating one then achieves free passage.

This refers to the fifth line. With firmness occupying its proper position and having a correspondent, it is not blocked or overbearing. Since retreat is not blocked or overbearing, one can act in accordance with the time.

The way of yin is about to gradually grow, yet the correct way has not yet been entirely extinguished, hence 'Small Benefit in Correctness.'

lines.2: Dwelling within and occupying the central position, this line is the host of retreat — all things retreat from it. How can it hold them fast? If one can hold to the way of principled centrality, solidity, and compliance to secure them, then none can prevail in loosening it.
lines.3: Being within and close to the second line, yang attaches to yin. One ought to retreat, yet one is tethered, hence it says 'tethered retreat.' The meaning of retreat is that one ought to keep far from petty people. By yang attaching to yin, one is tethered to one's place and cannot distance oneself from harm — one is already exhausted. It is fitting that there should be humiliation and perilous dan
lines.4:
Positioned in the outer trigram yet having a correspondent in the inner, the superior person excels at retreat and thus can let go of it. The petty person clings and is attached, and therefore is blocked.

lines.5: Retreating yet attaining correctness, one exercises control back over the inner. The petty person obeys the command and follows in rectifying his intentions. Not with hatred but with dignity — attaining the auspiciousness of correctness, this is the admirableness of retreat.
lines.6: Positioned at the outermost extreme, with no correspondent within, one rises above and severs all ties. The heart has no doubts or backward glances. Worries and troubles cannot weigh upon one; stringed arrows cannot reach one. This is why bountiful retreat has nothing that is not beneficial.

hexagrams.name: Great Power

wangbi.judgment:
"The great" refers to the yang lines. The petty way is about to be extinguished, and the great obtains correctness—hence Benefit in Correctness.

The nature of Heaven and Earth is simply correctness and greatness. When one broadens correctness and extends greatness to the utmost, then the nature of Heaven and Earth can be perceived.

lines.1: One who attains Great Vigor must be able to achieve success naturally. There has never been one who encroached upon others yet managed to sustain his vigor to the end. lines.2: It occupies the central position. A yang line dwelling in a yin place treads with humility and is not overbearing—hence Correctness brings good fortune.
lines.3: It occupies the extreme of the firm, a yang line in a yang position—this is one who employs vigor. Therefore the petty person uses it to display vigor, while the noble person uses it as a net that ensnares himself. To take vigor as one's standard of correctness brings danger. lines.4: The firm lines below advance upward, which will bring worry and apprehension. Yet with a yang line dwelling in a yin position, one's conduct does not violate humility. Not losing one's vigor, one therefore attains Correctness and good fortune, and regret vanishes. Having attained vigor, the yin lines above do not ensnare one's path—hence the fence breaks open and there is no entanglement. With vig
lines.5: Dwelling in Great Vigor, even a yang line in a yang position cannot escape blame—how much more so for a yin line in a yang position, the soft riding atop the firm? "Ram" symbolizes vigor. One will inevitably lose one's ram and forfeit one's position. If one can relinquish vigor with ease, rather than amid peril and difficulty, then one attains no regret. lines.6: It has a corresponding line in the third—hence it cannot retreat. It fears the growth of the firm—hence it cannot advance. hexagrams.name: Progress

wangbi.judgment:
In general, when it speaks of 'going upward,' it means one's destination is a position of honor.

Kang is a term of praise. To be compliant and thereby manifest brightness—this is the Way of a minister. When the soft advances and goes upward, all things support it. Therefore it receives the bestowal of horses in abundant multitude. In the case of Hexagram Song (Conflict), one receives official vestments only to have them stripped away three times before the morning ends. When the soft advances and receives favor, it is received three times in a single day.

lines.1: Situated at the beginning of the compliant trigram and corresponding to the start of the bright trigram, the virtue of brightness and compliance will flourish from here. Advancing toward brightness and retreating into compliance, one does not lose what is correct; therefore it says 'advancing, yet pushed back—correctness brings good fortune.' Positioned at the start of the hexagram, one's merits a
lines.2: Advancing without a corresponding line above, one's virtue is not made manifest; therefore it says 'advancing, yet sorrowful.' Occupying the central position and attaining the proper place, treading in compliance and correctness, one does not turn back one's resolve because of lacking a corresponding line—this is one who, dwelling in obscurity, is able to bring forth sincerity. Cultivating virtue
lines.3: Occupying a position that is not proper to it—this is cause for regret. Yet its aspiration is to go upward; it shares trust with the multitude; it is compliant and attaches itself to brightness. Therefore it is able to have its regret vanish.
lines.4: It treads in a position that is not proper to it; above it serves the Fifth, below it sits atop three yin lines. Treading in a position not proper to it, it both carries a burden and rides in a carriage—it has no established achievement in which to find security, and its aspiration has nothing to rely upon. To advance under such conditions is truly a danger even when correct. Advancing like a hams
lines.5: The soft obtains the honored position; a yin line serves as the enlightened ruler, able to refrain from employing scrutiny and not taking over the duties of those below. hexagrams.name: Opposition

wangbi.judgment:
When all affairs are mutually contrary, this is the way of harm — how then can small matters be fortunate? It is because these three virtues are present.

The time of opposition and separation is not something a petty person can make use of.

lines.1: Occupying the beginning of Kui, dwelling at the bottom of the lower trigram, without a responsive counterpart and standing alone — this is cause for regret. Yet it shares its will with the fourth line, and therefore regret vanishes. A horse is a thing that necessarily stands out. At the beginning of things, amid divergence one loses one's horse, but nothing can conceal it in private — it will inev
lines.2: Occupying a position in Kui while out of one's proper place, one is about to have nowhere to find rest. Yet the fifth line has also lost its proper place; both seek their kindred, going out and heading the same way, meeting unexpectedly — hence it says 'meets the master in an alleyway.' In the time of Kui one has found an ally; although one has lost one's position, one has not lost the Way.
lines.3: In general, when things are near yet do not get along, there is misfortune. In the time of Kui, this line treads in a position that is not its own — yin occupying a yang place, the yielding riding atop the firm. Its will is set on what is above, yet it does not harmonize with the fourth line. The second responds to the fifth, so though near, they do not bond. Hence one sees the carriage dragged ba
lines.4: Without a responsive counterpart, dwelling alone — the fifth responds on its own to the second, and the third is in opposition with this line. Hence it says 'opposed and isolated.' The first line likewise has no responsive counterpart and stands alone. In the time of Kui, both stand in isolation; both occupy the lower part of their respective trigrams and share the same will. Yet this line has los
lines.5: Not in its proper position — hence regret. Having a responsive counterpart — hence it vanishes. 'Its kinsman' refers to the second line. 'Biting through the skin' means gnawing through what is yielding. Although the third line is adjacent to the second, what the second bites through does not obstruct this line's responsive bond. Going forward under these conditions, what blame could there be? Goin
lines.6: Occupying the extreme of Kui, the way of opposition has not yet opened — hence 'opposed and isolated.' This line dwells at the extreme of flame, while the third line occupies the fullness of the marsh — this is the extreme of opposition. Viewing the most defiled of things from the extreme of civilized brightness — this is the utmost of opposition. A pig covered in mud — nothing could be filthier.

hexagrams.name: Obstruction

en: ' As the master of the lower trigram, this is what the inner [trigram] relies upon

wangbi.judgment:
The southwest is the earth. The northeast is the mountain. If one takes difficulty toward level ground, the difficulty is resolved; if one takes difficulty toward the mountain, the way is exhausted.

Going forth, one achieves deliverance.

The lines all occupy their proper positions, each treading its correct place. Dwelling in difficulty and treading correctness—this is the Way of ordering the state. When the correct Way has not yet been blocked, difficulty is overcome through correctness; therefore correctness brings good fortune. If one encounters difficulty and loses correctness, how can good fortune be obtained?

lines.1: Situated at the beginning of difficulty, dwelling at the start of stopping, one alone perceives what lies ahead, sees danger and stops, waiting for the right time—how wise indeed! Therefore going forth encounters obstruction, while turning back gains praise.
lines.2: In a time of dwelling in difficulty*, one treads in the proper position, dwells without losing the center, and responds to the fifth line. One does not, because the fifth is amid difficulty, act selfishly to keep oneself distant from harm. Holding fast with unwavering heart, one's resolve is to assist the royal house. Therefore it says: 'The king's minister struggles through obstruction upon obstr
lines.3: Advancing, one enters danger; turning back, one attains one's position. Therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction; turning back, one returns.' As the master of the lower trigram, this is what the inner [trigram] relies upon.
lines.4: Going forth, there is no corresponding line; turning back, one rides upon the strong. Going and coming are both difficult; therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction, turning back one joins.' Attaining one's position and treading correctly, fulfilling one's fundamental substance—though encountering difficulty, it is not something recklessly brought upon oneself.
lines.5: In a time of dwelling in difficulty, alone amid danger—this is the greatest of difficulties; therefore it says 'great obstruction.' Yet dwelling without losing correctness, treading without losing the center, holding fast to virtue's constancy, and not changing one's integrity—being thus, those of like mind gather and arrive; therefore it says 'companions come.'
lines.6:
Going forth prolongs difficulty; turning back brings difficulty to its end. When difficulty ends, all obstructions are overcome, and one's resolve is greatly fulfilled; therefore it says 'going forth meets obstruction; turning back brings greatness—good fortune.' When danger is leveled and difficulty resolved, the great Way can flourish; therefore it says 'benefit in seeing a great person.'

hexagrams.name: Deliverance

wangbi.judgment:
The southwest represents the multitude. Releasing difficulty and crossing through danger benefits being extended to the multitude. It also does not bring hardship in the northeast, which is why it does not say 'no benefit in the northeast.'

There has never been one skilled at releasing difficulty who was confused about dwelling in peace. The meaning of Release is releasing difficulty and relieving distress. If there is no difficulty requiring one to go and resolve it, then returning preserves the center. If there is difficulty requiring one to go, then swiftness brings good fortune. Without difficulty, one can restore one's center; with difficulty, one can relieve the distress.

lines.1: Release means untying. What was obstructed in difficulty and tangled together is here released. Situated at the very beginning when hardship and difficulty first begin to dissolve, at the juncture when the firm and the yielding first begin to disperse, offenses and distress are about to be pardoned, thereby leveling the danger. At such a time, one need not be troubled about one's position and is w
lines.2: The fox is a creature that hides and lurks. Being firm and central with a corresponding line, it is entrusted by the Fifth. Situated within the danger, it knows the conditions of danger. Resolving things by this means, it can catch what is hidden and lurking; therefore it says 'in the hunt, three foxes are caught.' Yellow is a designation for the center of principle. Arrow (shi) means straight. Hu

lines.5: Occupying the honored position, treading in the center, and corresponding with the firm, it can achieve release and obtain good fortune. It has lost its position and carries a burden while riding, and it occupies the top of the lower trigram; therefore it is called the 'high wall.' hexagrams.name: Decrease

wangbi.judgment:
Gen is the yang trigram; Dui is the yin trigram. In general, yin is compliant toward yang. Yang stops above, yin is joyful and compliant — decreasing the lower to benefit the upper: this is the meaning of "moving upward."

The Way of Decrease is to decrease the lower to benefit the upper, to decrease the firm to benefit the yielding. Decreasing the lower to benefit the upper is not supplementing what is insufficient; decreasing the firm to benefit the yielding is not fostering the Way of the noble person. To practice Decrease and yet be able to obtain good fortune — only through sincerity is this possible! If one decreases with sincerity, then there is Sublime Beginning good fortune, no blame with Correctness possible, and it is Beneficial to have somewhere to go. Decreasing the firm to benefit the yielding does not aim to eliminate firmness; decreasing the lower to benefit the upper does not aim to surfeit the upper. If decreasing firmness does not lead to deviancy, and benefiting the upper does not constitute flattery, then what blame is there that Correctness could address? Even if one cannot rescue from great calamity, proceeding in this way, nothing will resist.

"He" (曷) is an interrogative particle. "What shall one use" means: what need is there for lavishness?

Two bamboo bowls are vessels of plain and modest quality. Practicing Decrease with sincerity, even two bamboo bowls may be used for the offering.

The Way of utmost frugality cannot be constant.

The lower does not dare to be rigid, valuing upward service — this is what is called "decreasing the firm to benefit the yielding." Firmness is the chief of virtues; decreasing it cannot be made constant.

The natural endowment of things determines each one's proper measure. What is short should not be considered insufficient; what is long should not be considered excessive. What could Decrease and Increase add to this? It is not a constant principle of the Way, therefore it must move together with the time.

lines.1: The Way of Decrease is to decrease the lower to benefit the upper, to decrease the firm to benefit the yielding, in response to the demands of the time. Occupying the lowest position and decreasing firmness to serve yielding, one must not be idle. Being at the beginning of Decrease, one must not be complacent. wangbi.judgment:
Through the compliance of Xun one can ascend. Yet the yang line does not occupy the honored position and lacks the correctness of stern firmness, so one is not free from worry. Therefore, by seeing a great person, one is freed from anxiety.

Only after there is trust can one attain Sublime Beginning, Success, Benefit, Correctness, and the vanishing of regret. If after the day is done there is still no trust, then the revolution is not appropriate. The arising of regret and distress is born from change and movement. When the revolution is appropriate, then regret vanishes.

hexagrams.name: Keeping Still

wangbi.judgment:
The Way of stopping cannot be constantly employed; it must be applied when one cannot proceed. When it fits the timing, the Way is bright and luminous.

Changing 'back' to 'stopping' clarifies that the back is where stopping applies. Stopping cannot be applied to the face; it can be applied to the back. Applying stopping where stopping is due, not applying stopping where action is due—this is finding its proper place. Therefore it says: stopping at the point of stopping means stopping in its proper place.

lines.1: Dwelling at the beginning of stopping, there is nowhere to go by moving; therefore stopping at the toes brings no blame. Being utterly still and settled, therefore there is Benefit in lasting Correctness.
lines.2: "What follows" refers to the toes. Stopping the calves means the toes cannot be lifted. The calves are restless in nature yet are placed in stillness; unable to lift what follows, and also unable to withdraw and listen in quiet composure, therefore one's heart is not glad.
lines.3: "Waist" (xian) is the middle of the body. The third line falls at the juncture of the two trigram images; therefore it says "keeping still at the waist." "Yin" (yi) refers to the flesh along the middle of the spine. Stopping is imposed upon the body at its center, dividing the body; therefore the flesh of the spine is split apart and the worry of danger sears the heart. The meaning of Gen is that
lines.4:
The middle and upper portions are called the body. Treading in one's proper position, one seeks to stop within one's own body and finds one's proper place; therefore one does not fall into blame.

One stops at one's own person without dividing the whole body.
lines.5:
Applying stopping to the jaws, and dwelling in the center, one's mouth has no ill-chosen words and is able to make regret vanish.

Being able to employ centrality and correctness, therefore words are well-ordered.
lines.6: Dwelling at the extreme of stopping, this is the utmost of stopping. Generous and weighty in the uppermost position, one does not fall into error or recklessness; it is fitting that there be auspiciousness.

hexagrams.name: Development

wangbi.judgment: Jian is the hexagram of gradual advance. Stillness combined with compliance — by these means one proceeds forward; this is gradual advance. Because stillness and compliance constitute the mode of advance, the woman's marriage is auspicious. Because one advances while employing Correctness, there is Benefit in Correctness.

lines.1: The hong is a water bird. In the meaning of proceeding to advance, it begins from below and ascends, hence the wild goose is used as a metaphor. All six lines take advancing and treading upon their position as their meaning. Beginning to advance yet positioned at the very bottom, with no corresponding line above — it is like treading upon the riverbank, dangerous and unable to find security. Begin
lines.2: Pan is a stable mountain rock. Advancing and attaining one's position, dwelling in the center with a corresponding line — originally without salary or sustenance, but advancing and obtaining them. The resulting joy and happiness surpass all other wishes.
lines.3: Lu is the top of the heights. Advancing to reach the plateau, it finds mutual affinity with the fourth line and cannot turn back. The husband goes on campaign and does not return, delighting in an improper union; the wife then also cannot maintain her fidelity. Pregnant by one who is not her husband, she therefore does not give birth. The third line originally belongs to the Gen trigram body, yet
lines.4: A bird going to a tree finds what is suitable for it. 'Perhaps finding a flat branch to perch on' means encountering a safe roosting place. Although it rides above the firm line, their intentions find mutual affinity.
lines.5: Ling (hilltop) is next in elevation after the plateau. Advancing and attaining the central position, yet separated by the third and fourth lines, unable to unite with its corresponding line — hence the wife does not conceive for three years. Each treads upon what is correct and dwells in the center; the third and fourth lines cannot long obstruct their path. After no more than three years, one wil
lines.6: Advancing to dwell in a lofty and pure place, unburdened by official position, nothing can bend its heart or disorder its will. Towering, pure, and transcendent, its deportment is worthy of esteem. Hence it says 'its feathers can be used as ceremonial ornaments, auspicious.'

hexagrams.judgment: The maiden's marriage resolves well. Sustained orientation is supported.
hexagrams.image: On the mountain, a tree: development. The realized person accordingly dwells in worthy character and improves the customs.

hexagrams.name: The Marrying Maiden

wangbi.judgment: 'Maiden' (mei) is a term for a younger sister. Dui is the youngest yin; Zhen is the eldest yang. The youngest yin serves the eldest yang — joyousness leading to movement — this is the image of marrying off a younger sister.

lines.1: A youngest daughter paired with the eldest son — this is not what is meant by an equal match; it is the meaning of following as a secondary bride. 'Maiden' (mei) is a term for a younger sister. In the conduct of a younger sister, nothing is as good as serving as a secondary bride. Just as an heir who is the ruler's son, though young, does not act recklessly — so a younger sister serving as a secon
lines.2: Although it has lost its proper position, it dwells within and occupies the center. The one-eyed can still see — this is sufficient to preserve constancy. Being within and treading in the center, and able to keep to constancy, hence it is beneficial for a secluded person's Correctness.
lines.3: The mistress of the household still remains, yet she seeks to advance. The advance does not meet the right time, hence there is waiting. She cannot advance, so she returns to wait for the right time, and only then goes forth as a secondary bride.
lines.4: To go to another with an improper position and no corresponding line — one must wait until the other's way is exhausted and there is no one else to engage with, and only then can one go. Hence delaying the date and postponing the marriage, waiting for the right time.
lines.5: 'Sleeves' (mei) are the garment sleeves used for ceremonial deportment. 'The sovereign's sleeves' refers to the one favored by Di Yi, which is the fifth line. Being adorned and honored by Di Yi, hence it is called 'the sovereign's sleeves.' Her match is at Nine in the Second. Dui is the youngest and Zhen is the eldest; for the eldest to follow the youngest is not as fine as for the youngest to fol
lines.6: The sheep refers to the third line. Occupying the extremity of the hexagram, looking up there is nothing to receive from above, and below there is no corresponding line. As a woman receiving a command, the basket is empty and nothing is given to her. As a man issuing a command downward, one slaughters the sheep but there is no blood. Slaughtering the sheep with no blood means there is no response

hexagrams.name: Abundance

wangbi.judgment:
What is great and successful is what the king can attain.

The meaning of Feng is to broaden and expand what is subtle and minute, and to open up what is hidden and stagnant. To be the sovereign of all under heaven while allowing the subtle and hidden not to attain success means that worry has not yet ceased. Therefore, only upon attaining abundance and success can one be free from worry. Employing the virtue of abundance, success, and freedom from worry, one should dwell at the center of heaven to illuminate everywhere. Therefore it says 'it is fitting to be like the sun at midday.'

lines.1:
Dwelling at the beginning of Feng, its counterpart is in the fourth position. Yang going to yang, brilliance joined with movement—they are able to magnify and enlarge each other. Xun means 'equal.' Though equal, there is no blame; to go forth brings esteem. The first and fourth are both yang lines; hence they are called equal.

If equality is exceeded, there is contention; in their interaction, th
lines.2: Bu is a covering that dims and obstructs light—a thing that blocks radiance. Dwelling in a time of brilliance and movement yet unable to make oneself abundant through the virtue of radiant greatness—already situated within the inner trigram, and moreover a yin line dwelling in a yin position—what is made abundant is the screen, dark with nothing visible. Hence it says 'he makes abundant his screen
lines.3: Pei is a pennant curtain, used to ward off bright light. Mei is a faint, dim illumination. Its correspondence is with Top Six; its inclination is toward yin. Though better than a yin line dwelling in a yin position, it is still insufficient to escape darkness. What is made abundant is the curtain; this is what 'at midday he sees tiny stars' means. In applying brilliance, one merely sees tiny stars
lines.4: A yang line dwelling in a yin position—this is making abundant his screen of grass. Obtaining the first line to bring forth brilliance—the equal lord brings good fortune.
lines.5: With the substance of yin, it comes to take up the honored yang position. Able to make itself radiant and great, it makes its virtue luminous and manifest, thereby obtaining celebration and praise.
lines.6: Wu (roof/house) is a thing that shelters and shades. A yin line dwelling at the extreme and furthest outside, not treading upon a proper position—one who deeply hides oneself in seclusion, cutting off all traces and concealing oneself in the depths. Having made abundant his roof and further screened his household—the roof thick and the household covered—the darkness is extreme. Though one peers th

hexagrams.name: The Gentle

wangbi.judgment:
Taking Xun (compliance) entirely as its virtue, therefore it achieves only small success. Both upper and lower trigrams are Xun, so none disobey the commands, and thus orders are carried out. Therefore, at the time of reiterating commands and carrying out affairs, those above and below cannot but be compliant.

When one proceeds with compliance and deference, nothing resists.

When a great person employs this, the Way flourishes all the more.

lines.1:
Situated at the beginning of the command, this is one who cannot yet submit to the command, hence the advancing and retreating. To enforce commands and bring the deviant into line, nothing is better than a military person—hence the benefit in a military person's correctness to bring order.

With a disposition of compliant submission, one advances and retreats in doubt and apprehension.
lines.2: Situated at the center of the Xun trigram, already in a lower position, and further having a yang line occupying a yin position—the humility and compliance are extreme. Hence it says 'compliant beneath the bed.' When humility is extreme and correctness is lost, one falls into blame and error. If one can, by virtue of occupying the central position, direct this utmost humility toward the spirits an
lines.3: 'Pin' (頻) means furrowed and frowning—unhappy and exhausted, referring to what is done out of compulsion. Being firm and correct yet ridden upon by the fourth line, its intent is exhausted and yet it must comply. This is why there is humiliation.
lines.4: Riding upon the firm is cause for regret. However, it obtains its proper position and serves the fifth line; in its humility it finds one to serve. Although the yielding controls the firm, it relies on the honored one and treads on correctness. Using this to carry out commands, it will surely be able to capture the violent and keep the inhumane at a distance. For catching game that is beneficial,
lines.5: Having a yang line occupy a yang position diminishes humble compliance. Yet by holding to centrality and correctness to proclaim commands, nothing disobeys—hence it says 'correctness brings auspiciousness, regret vanishes, nothing is unfavorable.' When transformation does not proceed gradually and one abruptly applies firmness and directness to things, at first none are pleased—hence 'no beginning
lines.6: Situated at the extreme of Xun, the compliance is excessive and goes too far—hence it says 'compliant beneath the bed.' The axe is that by which one cuts decisively. Excessive compliance loses correctness, and one loses the means to cut decisively—hence it says 'loses the resources and the axe; correctness brings misfortune.'

hexagrams.judgment: Small fulfillment. Going forward is supported. Seeing the great person is supported.
hexagrams.image: Following winds: the gentle. The realized person accordingly reiterates commands and carries out undertakings.

hexagrams.name: Dispersion

en: As the master of Dispersion, only the king may dwell in this position, and only then is there no blame

wangbi.judgment:
The second line, being firm, comes to dwell on the inside and is not exhausted by danger. The fourth line, being yielding, obtains its position on the outside and is in accord with those above. The firm within faces no difficulty of danger and entrapment; the yielding outside faces no discord of opposition and rebellion—hence there is Success, it is beneficial to cross the great river, and beneficial to be correct. In general, when the firm achieves free expression without the encumbrance of fear and crookedness, and the yielding treads upon correctness and shares its purpose with the firm, then in all cases there is Success, benefit in crossing the great river, and benefit in correctness.

The king is thereby in the midst of Dispersion, hence he can establish the ancestral temple.

Riding on wood means crossing through difficulty. Wood is specifically the means for crossing the river. To cross difficulty while constantly using the Way of Dispersion will certainly bring success.

lines.1:
Huan means to scatter. Being at the beginning of scattering, the divergence and dispersal are not yet severe; hence one can travel freely, attaining one's purpose while avoiding difficulty. One does not wait until the danger is extreme before fleeing; hence it says 'using rescue, the horse is strong—auspicious.'

Observing the difficulty and then acting, not contending with danger—hence it says 'c
lines.2: Ji (bench) is that which supports things—it refers to the first line. The second line has no corresponding line, and is paired with the first. The first obtains the Way of Dispersion; scattering and rushing, it finds its place of rest. Hence regret vanishes.
lines.3: The meaning of Dispersion is that the inside is dangerous while the outside is secure. Dispersing one's own self with one's purpose directed outward, not clinging stubbornly to what one holds, and sharing purpose with the firm—hence one attains no regret.
lines.4: Having crossed beyond danger and difficulty, obtaining its position and embodying Xun (compliance), sharing its purpose with the fifth line, inwardly managing confidential affairs and outwardly proclaiming transformative commands—hence it is able to disperse the group's dangers and thereby make its Way shine. However, being in a lowly and compliant position, it cannot act on its own authority. In
lines.5:
Occupying the honored position and treading upon correctness, dwelling in the center of Xun (compliance), sweating forth the great proclamation to sweep away dangers and hardships. As the master of Dispersion, only the king may dwell in this position, and only then is there no blame.

The correct position cannot be lent to another.
lines.6: Ti means distant. Being farthest from harm and not close to aggression and attack, one disperses one's grief and sorrow and goes far away. Dispersing troubles in a place far from harm—who would assign blame!

hexagrams.judgment: Fulfillment. The king approaches the ancestral temple. Crossing the great river is supported. Sustained orientation is supported.
hexagrams.image: Wind moves over water: dispersion. The ancient kings accordingly made offerings to heaven and established temples.

hexagrams.name: Limitation

en: Occupying the proper position and dwelling in the center, as the master of regulation one does not lose the mean

wangbi.judgment:
Kan is yang and Dui is yin. Yang is above and yin is below; the firm and yielding are distinguished. When firm and yielding are distinguished without disorder, and the firm attains the center to serve as the master of regulation, this is the meaning of jie. The greatest form of regulation is none other than the distinction of firm and yielding, the differentiation of male and female.

When regulation becomes excessively bitter, then things cannot endure it. When things cannot endure it, then it cannot be maintained as correct.

Only then does it lead to success. Without joy yet traversing danger, exceeding the center in making regulations—then the Way reaches exhaustion.

lines.1: Being at the beginning of Regulation, this is one who will bring order to what has been scattered and establish institutional measures. Therefore one discerns clearly between what is open and what is blocked, considers carefully the dangers of deception, does not go out through the door of the courtyard, and maintains cautious secrecy without lapse. Only then are affairs brought to completion with
lines.2: The first line has already created the regulations; by the time one reaches the second, it is fitting to promulgate those measures. Yet one deliberately conceals them, missing the critical moment to the utmost degree, and consequently they fall into neglect. Therefore, not going out through the gate of the courtyard leads to misfortune.
lines.3: Ruo is a particle. Occupying a yang position with a yin line, and a yielding line riding atop a firm line, one violates the Way of regulation to the point of mournful lamentation. This is brought about by oneself; there is no one else to blame. Hence it says 'no blame.'
lines.4: Having attained the proper position and being compliant, one does not alter one's regulation and is thereby able to achieve success. Serving the one above in this manner, one attains the Way.
lines.5: Occupying the proper position and dwelling in the center, as the master of regulation one does not lose the mean. This is what is meant by 'not wasting resources and not harming the people.' To regulate without bitterness—if not sweet, then what? Proceeding forth by this method, going forth there is esteem.
lines.6: Exceeding the center of regulation to the point of reaching the utmost extreme—this is bitter regulation. If one applies this to governing others*, things cannot endure it; this is the misfortune of correctness. If one applies this to cultivating oneself, one's conduct is free from recklessness, and therefore regret vanishes.

hexagrams.judgment: Fulfillment. Bitter limitation cannot be sustained.
hexagrams.image: Water above the lake: limitation. The realized person accordingly creates measures and standards, and examines the nature of character and conduct.

Not going out past the gate and courtyard. Adverse.

hexagrams.name: Before Completion

en: Dwelling in the honored position with yielding, situated at the fullness of cultural brilliance, serving as the ruler of Not Yet Across—therefore one must be correct and only then is there good fortune

wangbi.judgment:
By dwelling in the center with yielding, it does not oppose the firm. Being able to receive the firm and strong, it therefore attains success.

A small fox cannot wade across a great river; it must wait until the water is nearly gone before it can cross. In the time of Not Yet Across, one must be firm and strong to extricate from difficulty, and only then can one cross. Crossing only when nearly done, it has not yet emerged from the midst of danger.

A small fox, though able to cross, has no strength to spare. About to cross yet wetting its tail, its strength is exhausted at this point and it cannot continue to the end. The danger and difficulty are still not enough to be crossed. One who would cross what is Not Yet Across must have strength to spare.

The positions are not proper, therefore it is Not Yet Across. The firm and yielding correspond, therefore it can be crossed.

lines.1: Situated at the beginning of Not Yet Across, dwelling at the very bottom of danger—one who cannot cross. Yet wishing to go to its correspondent, advancing would drown the self. The beginning of Not Yet Across begins from the Top Six of Already Across. If wetting the head still does not make one turn back, and it reaches the point of wetting the tail, this shows one who does not know where to stop.
lines.2: Its substance is firm and it treads the center, corresponding with the fifth. The fifth is yin and yielding in substance, corresponding with and relying upon it rather than taking charge itself. Dwelling in the time of Not Yet Across, situated in the midst of danger, with the quality of firm centrality, it is entrusted and relied upon to rescue from peril and manage difficulties amid distress and
lines.3: With the quality of yin, it has lost its proper position and dwells in danger—one who cannot save itself. With an improper position, its strength is insufficient to save itself; if it seeks to advance, it will lose its life. Hence it says 'to advance brings misfortune.' The second is able to rescue from difficulty, and this line is close beside it. If one abandons self-reliance and entrusts onesel
lines.4: Situated in the time of Not Yet Across, having emerged above the danger, dwelling at the beginning of cultural brilliance, with a firm quality of substance, and close to the supreme ruler. Although it treads a position that is not its own, its resolve is set upon correctness, and thus it is fortunate and regret vanishes. Its resolve is carried out and nothing restrains its awesome power, hence it
lines.5: Dwelling in the honored position with yielding, situated at the fullness of cultural brilliance, serving as the ruler of Not Yet Across—therefore one must be correct and only then is there good fortune; with good fortune one then attains no regret. Now, with the quality of yielding compliance and cultural brilliance, dwelling in the honored position, delegating to the capable without laboring ones
lines.6: At the extreme of Not Yet Across, it reverts to Already Across. The Way of Already Across is that those entrusted with responsibilities are fitting. When those entrusted are fitting, one can trust them without doubt and enjoy leisure oneself. Hence it says 'there is sincerity in drinking wine, no blame.' Because one is able to trust others, one attains ease and comfort without worrying that affair
